back: A map showing the distribution of one topic or statistic, e.g. rainfall or population density.
Areas shaded by class of a rate or density, darker = higher; hides variation within areas.
Lines of equal value: contour (height), isohyet (rainfall), isotherm (temperature), isobar (pressure).
Circle area ∝ value, so radius ∝ √value: a quarter of the value → half the radius.
Each dot = a fixed quantity placed where items are; shows clustering, but dots merge where values are high.
Flow lines follow routes, width = volume. Desire lines are straight origin-destination lines.
The area from which a settlement or service draws its users.
Area rates → choropleth; point data that varies gradually → isolines; movement → flow or desire lines; values at places → proportional symbols.
